findings.issue_text: **1. `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — `prisma` is used but never imported.**
**2. `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-108` — the refreshed token is fetched, persisted, and then discarded.**
**3. `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101` — the zod `safeParse` *wrapper* is written to `credential.key`, corrupting the credential.**

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `SafeParseSuccess` object (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29`), not the parsed data. The previous code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, i.e. the data itself. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`, and the next call to `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws — Google Calendar is permanently broken for that user until they reconnect. Note the other two callers use it correctly (`tokenResponse.data`, `accessTokenParsed.data`), which confirms this is the outlier.
**4. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59` — the team admin check is unreachable; any team member can install team-wide app credentials.**
**5. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27` — a placeholder string overwrites the real refresh token.**

This runs on both branches. In sync mode `minimumTokenResponseSchema` strips everything except `access_token`, so `refresh_token` is always absent and always set to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Office 365 then does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264`) and persists it — the user's genuine long-lived refresh token is destroyed in the database. It is not recoverable, so an operator who later disables credential sync finds every Office 365 credential permanently dead with no error surfaced. The same hazard exists in non-sync mode wherever the provider schema marks `refresh_token` optional (it is optional at `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:56`) and the provider omits it on a given refresh.
**6. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-19` — the sync branch and the fallback branch return incompatible types, breaking sync for Google and HubSpot.**

`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-95`: the fallback returns a Gaxios response and the caller reads `res?.data`. In sync mode `res` is a `Response`, `res.data` is `undefined`, and `token.access_token` throws a `TypeError`. The `catch` at line 104 only special-cases `"invalid_grant"`, so the refresh silently no-ops and the user's calendar quietly stops working.

`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-203`: the result is *asserted* as `HubspotToken`. In sync mode `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is `undefined` → `expiryDate` becomes `NaN`, and a `Response` object is serialized into `credential.key`. The `catch` at line 204 swallows it with a log line.
**7. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11` — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not do what its comments claim.**

`z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string `"[object Object]"`, as does the second expression, so the second computed key silently overwrites the first. The resulting schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. Neither "any property with a number is the expiry" nor "allow other properties" is implemented — and because `z.object` strips unknown keys, **the expiry field is discarded on every sync-mode refresh**. Downstream expiry checks (`isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)` at `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:279`) then see a stale or missing expiry and refresh on every single call.

For the four "no" rows, the strict provider schema is still applied to the minimal sync response and rejects it — e.g. `webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88` requires `scope` and `token_type` as `z.literal(...)` plus `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`, none of which the documented sync response contains, so it always fails with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Salesforce gets the relaxed parsing but never routes through the sync endpoint at all. Net effect: the headline feature works end-to-end for Office 365 Calendar only.
**9. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15` — the outbound sync call is unauthenticated and unvalidated.**
**10. `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31, 57-59` — unhandled throws become 500s on attacker-reachable paths.**
**11. `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-80` — `findFirst` picks an arbitrary credential and never clears `invalid`.**

Two problems. First, a user may legitimately hold multiple credentials for the same `appId` (e.g. two connected Google Calendar accounts); `findFirst` with no ordering or disambiguator overwrites a non-deterministic one, silently clobbering the wrong account's keys. Second, `GoogleCalendarService` sets `invalid: true` on a credential when a refresh fails (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:107-112`); the sync update writes only `key`, so a credential repaired by the parent application stays flagged invalid and continues to be skipped. That defeats the main recovery path the feature exists to provide.
**12. `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29` — secret comparison is non-constant-time and fails open if misconfigured.**
**13. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9` — unguarded `JSON.parse` of an attacker-controlled query param with a bare type assertion.**

`JSON.parse(req.query.state)` throws on any non-JSON `state`, and every OAuth callback in this PR calls it before any error handling — a crafted `?state=abc` on a public callback URL is an easy unhandled 500. The `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState` annotation is a compile-time assertion only, so `state.teamId` reaching `prisma.team.findFirst({ where: { id: state.teamId } })` in `createOAuthAppCredential.ts:34` is entirely unvalidated — a string or object there produces a Prisma runtime error. Stripe's own callback already defends against this shape of problem with a `try/catch` (`stripepayment/api/callback.ts:12-16`), which shows the hazard was known.

**15. `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` — unexplained regression from `${appConfig.slug}` to a hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"`.** `appConfig` is still imported and used on lines 12 and 22, so this just reintroduces a magic string that can drift from `config.json` and desync the registered OAuth redirect URI. It is also a template literal with no interpolation. Unrelated to the PR's stated intent — revert it.

**16. `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264` — diagnostics lost, dead guard left behind.** The removed `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", ..., "MS response:", responseJson)` was the only way to see *why* an Outlook refresh failed; the replacement throws a generic `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` with no context. Meanwhile `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` is now dead code, since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure. Log the zod issues inside the helper before throwing, and drop the residual `&&`.
**17. `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94` — unreachable branch.** `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` can never fire, for the same reason as #16.

**18. `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` — `response.statusText !== "OK"` is a fragile success check.** `statusText` is empty for HTTP/2 responses and is not a reliable success signal in `undici`. Use `if (!response.ok)` and include the status code in the error message.

**19. `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34` — over-fetching a sensitive row.** `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id } })` with no `select` pulls every column, including the password hash and 2FA secret, purely to test existence. Add `select: { id: true }`.

**21. Style/hygiene in the new files:** `createOAuthAppCredential.ts:6` imports via `"../oauth/decodeOAuthState"` from inside the `oauth/` directory itself — should be `"./decodeOAuthState"`; `createOAuthAppCredential.ts:37` re-reads `req.session?.user.id` when `userId` is already in scope and narrowed; `createOAuthAppCredential.ts:45` throws a bare `Error` where the surrounding code uses `HttpError` (so this surfaces as a 500 rather than a 403); `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13` takes `response: any`; `app-credential.ts:16` has an empty `/** */` doc comment.

**22. Documentation gap.** `.env.example` describes the variables but nothing specifies the contract a self-hoster must implement: the request shape sent to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, the expected response shape, or the encryption format for the webhook `keys` field (AES-256 mode, IV placement). Given this is aimed squarely at self-hosters, that contract needs to be written down somewhere durable. Worth also noting that team credentials (`userId === null`) silently bypass sync (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5`) and the webhook has no team path at all — intentional, probably, but undocumented.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

So the comments (“any property with a number is the expiry” and “allow other properties”) are not reflected by the actual schema and the schema will not behave as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For the four "no" rows, the strict provider schema is still applied to the minimal sync response and rejects it — e.g. `webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88` requires `scope` and `token_type` as `z.literal(...)` plus `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`, none of which the documented sync response contains, so it always fails with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Salesforce gets the relaxed parsing but never routes through the sync endpoint at all. Net effect: the headline feature works end-to-end for Office 365 Calendar only.
**9. `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15` — the outbound sync call is unauthenticated and unvalidated.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the code does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication material (no shared secret header, token, signature, etc.) and no response validation (it returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok`, status codes, or parsing/validating the payload). This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a real security/correctness concern for the sync path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **11. `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-80` — `findFirst` picks an arbitrary credential and never clears `invalid`.**

adjudication.rationale:
In the added `app-credential.ts`, the code does use `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })`, which would be arbitrary only if multiple matching credentials can exist. The diff does not show the Prisma schema or any guarantee/violation of uniqueness for `(userId, appId)`, so it’s not verifiable from this diff that this will pick the “wrong” credential.

The claim that it “never clears `invalid`” is also not grounded in the diff: no `invalid` field is referenced anywhere in this file, and the credential model shape isn’t shown. Whether such a field exists and must be cleared is speculative.

Therefore, this finding is not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two problems. First, a user may legitimately hold multiple credentials for the same `appId` (e.g. two connected Google Calendar accounts); `findFirst` with no ordering or disambiguator overwrites a non-deterministic one, silently clobbering the wrong account's keys. Second, `GoogleCalendarService` sets `invalid: true` on a credential when a refresh fails (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:107-112`); the sync update writes only `key`, so a credential repaired by the parent application stays flagged invalid and continues to be skipped. That defeats the main recovery path the feature exists to provide.
**12. `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29` — secret comparison is non-constant-time and fails open if misconfigured.**

adjudication.rationale: In `app-credential.ts` the webhook auth check is `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset/undefined (or empty in practice) and the request omits that header, both sides evaluate to `undefined`, the comparison is false, and the request is incorrectly accepted (fail-open on misconfiguration). Also, the direct `!==` string comparison is not constant-time, which can leak information via timing if an attacker can probe the endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` throws on any non-JSON `state`, and every OAuth callback in this PR calls it before any error handling — a crafted `?state=abc` on a public callback URL is an easy unhandled 500. Stripe's own callback already defends against this shape of problem with a `try/catch` (`stripepayment/api/callback.ts:12-16`), which shows the hazard was known.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **22. Documentation gap.** `.env.example` describes the variables but nothing specifies the contract a self-hoster must implement: the request shape sent to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, the expected response shape, or the encryption format for the webhook `keys` field (AES-256 mode, IV placement). Given this is aimed squarely at self-hosters, that contract needs to be written down somewhere durable. Worth also noting that team credentials (`userId === null`) silently bypass sync (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5`) and the webhook has no team path at all — intentional, probably, but undocumented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new self-hoster-facing env vars (CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET/HEADER_NAME, CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY) and new behaviors that require an external implementation, but the diff does not document the concrete contract those external systems must follow. In code, refreshOAuthTokens() POSTs URLSearchParams with keys {calcomUserId, appSlug} to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and returns the raw Response, while parseRefreshTokenResponse() conditionally validates only a minimal token shape (access_token plus numeric expiry-like fields) and even forces a dummy refresh_token when missing. Separately, the webhook decrypts reqBody.keys via symmetricDecrypt(..., CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY) then JSON.parse() it, but the encryption format details (mode/IV/encoding) are not specified anywhere in the diff. Also verifiable: refreshOAuthTokens() bypasses sync when userId is null (team credentials), and the webhook schema requires userId:int and has no team path. These are real, diff-visible documentation/contract gaps for the intended self-hoster audience.
